items: Type Safety: Only objects of a specific type can be added.
Eliminates Casting: No need to manually cast when retrieving objects.
Code Reusability: Same class/interface/method can be reused for different types.
Generic Algorithms: Algorithms can be created independently of specific data types.
When using Object type arrays or collections:
E – Element
T – Type
K – Key
V – Value
N – Number
Specific type is enforced at compile time.
Typecasting is not needed.
Incompatible types cause compilation errors, not runtime errors.

content.code: Student student = studentRecord.get(0); // No casting needed

items: Using a generic class without specifying a type:

content.code: Record record = new Record(); // Raw type

items: Drawbacks:
Use of raw types is discouraged except for backward compatibility.
Used in classes that deal with pairs or key-value relationships, like Map<K, V>.
Subtypes are not automatically compatible in generics.
Reason: Record<Student> is not a subtype of Record<Object>.
Cannot instantiate the type parameter:

content.code: E element = new E(); // Compilation error

items: Cannot extend Throwable:

content.code: class MyGenericException<T> extends Throwable { } // Not allowed

items: Cannot use primitive types: Must use wrapper classes (Integer, Double, Character, etc.)
